<!--
Pull requests should always be made for the `master` branch first, as that's
where development happens and the source of all future stable release branches.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed.

Do not create a pull request for stable branches unless the change is already
available in the `master` branch and it cannot be easily cherry-picked.
Alternatively, if the change is only relevant for that branch (e.g. rendering
fixes for the 3.2 branch).
-->
Fix #58840 
The return type for `limit_get` in Vulkan renderer and base renderer class was set to int, whereas all return values are unsigned ints. This caused weird bugs like the one described in the linked bug report. This patch takes care of that.

The return types have been fixed to `uint64_t` and should not overflow/cause any weird issues.
pr_comments:
One more thing, you also need to update the types used where ``limit_get()`` is called. For example, in shader_language.cpp the return value of ``limit_get`` is immediately placed into an ``int`` meaning that the issue reported in #58840 will still be present.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/51a00c2855009ce4cd6475c09209ebd22641f448/servers/rendering/shader_language.cpp#L7487
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/51a00c2855009ce4cd6475c09209ebd22641f448/servers/rendering/shader_language.cpp#L7496

Other places to check are:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ffd64505c51cb9734ad68f52277c807a9b759338/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/renderer_scene_gi_rd.cpp#L2456
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ffd64505c51cb9734ad68f52277c807a9b759338/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/renderer_canvas_render_rd.cpp#L2260
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1561737055bcececfd9661832665000dce7d61a9/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/renderer_storage_rd.cpp#L9965

There is another variable
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/51a00c2855009ce4cd6475c09209ebd22641f448/servers/rendering/shader_language.cpp#L7486
This gets compared to the `max_uniform_buffer_size` down in
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/51a00c2855009ce4cd6475c09209ebd22641f448/servers/rendering/shader_language.cpp#L7910

Does this needs to be changed to `uint64_t` as well or no?

> Does this needs to be changed to uint64_t as well or no? 

It depends. It will probably be fine (because it should never be negative), but for safety, it is best not to mix uints and ints.

There is another line which seems to be giving an issue
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c8fce1661da2ed02e94d3edd91fc3f31aa6888cc/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/renderer_scene_gi_rd.cpp#L2481
The `wg_todo` defined here
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c8fce1661da2ed02e94d3edd91fc3f31aa6888cc/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/renderer_scene_gi_rd.cpp#L2479
So I think this needs to be changed to a `uint64_t` as well?

> There is another line which seems to be giving an issue
> 
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c8fce1661da2ed02e94d3edd91fc3f31aa6888cc/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/renderer_scene_gi_rd.cpp#L2481
> 
> 
> The `wg_todo` defined here
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c8fce1661da2ed02e94d3edd91fc3f31aa6888cc/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/renderer_scene_gi_rd.cpp#L2479
> 
> 
> So I think this needs to be changed to a `uint64_t` as well?

Not ``uint64_t``. The underlying value is a ``uint32_t`` so it will likely be easier to just use an ``int64_t``. The code that uses ``wg_todo`` relies on it becoming negative in order to break a while loop, so you definitely do not want to use an unsigned value.
Thanks! And congrats for your first merged Godot contribution :tada:

issue_context.title: device limit exceeded for uniform buffer
comments: Do you have any global or per-instance uniforms defined in the project?

Looks like the ``maxUniformBufferRange`` is returning -1. 
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ffd64505c51cb9734ad68f52277c807a9b759338/drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_vulkan.cpp#L9343
the ``maxUniformBufferRange`` is set here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/1f3916e0b6afc84872f7354432ca8606d764fc22/drivers/vulkan/vulkan_context.cpp#L958
The ``maxUniformBufferRange`` for a 6700xt [as reported on GPUInfo.org](https://vulkan.gpuinfo.org/displayreport.php?id=14253#properties) is ``4,294,967,295`` which is the largest value an unsigned 32 bit integer can represent (conveniently ``vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties`` returns ``maxUniformBufferRange`` as a [uint32_t](https://www.khronos.org/registry/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/man/html/VkPhysicalDeviceLimits.html)). Converted to a signed 32 bit integer it is ``-1``

So the core of the problem is that ``limit_get`` returns an ``int`` even though many of the values it returns should be uints and require the full range of uint 
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ffd64505c51cb9734ad68f52277c807a9b759338/drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_vulkan.cpp#L9298

``limit_get`` should be changed to return a uint64_t (or a uint32_t if ``LIMIT_MIN_UNIFORM_BUFFER_OFFSET_ALIGNMENT`` is removed as it requires a uint64_t)
